growth_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to create a SendGrid account for transactional email (password resets, receipts, notifications). SendGrid is the specific vendor for this step.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already known: my company/business legal name, my primary domain, a support/contact email address I want tied to the account, an estimated monthly transactional email volume, and a brief description of our use case (e.g., 'password resets and order receipts for a SaaS product').

Then do the following:
1. Open SendGrid's signup page and begin the account creation form.
2. Fill in all fields that don't require payment or legal acceptance: company name, website/domain, email use case, estimated sending volume, and contact details, using the information I provided.
3. Note any required fields you cannot complete (e.g., billing/payment details, plan selection, or terms acceptance) and list them clearly for me.
4. Prepare a short summary of the plan tier that seems to fit our stated volume/use case, based on what's visible on the signup/pricing page, so I can review it.
5. Do NOT enter any payment or billing information, do NOT click 'Accept' on any Terms of Service or contract, and do NOT submit the final signup form.

When the form is filled out as far as possible, stop for human sign-off — I will personally review the pre-filled form, enter payment details, accept SendGrid's Terms of Service, and submit the signup.

Report back with: (a) confirmation of which fields were successfully pre-filled, (b) the list of remaining fields/actions that require my direct input (payment info, plan selection, terms acceptance), and (c) the plan tier recommendation summary, so I can complete and approve the signup myself.

growth_005:n2.prompt:
You are helping me authenticate my sending domain for transactional email through {{vendor}}. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my sending domain (e.g. mail.mydomain.com or my root domain), and (2) confirmation that {{vendor}} is the transactional email provider I've chosen, with my configured credentials already set up for their dashboard/API access.

Steps to take:
1. Using {{vendor}}'s domain authentication feature, generate the required SPF, DKIM, and (if offered) DMARC DNS records for my domain.
2. Compile these into a clear, ready-to-apply list: record type, host/name, and value for each.
3. Do NOT create or modify any DNS records yourself. Present the full list of records and a short summary of what authenticating this domain will change, then stop for human sign-off before any DNS changes are applied.
4. Once I confirm I've added the records (via my DNS host or if you have DNS access I've explicitly authorized), call {{vendor}}'s domain verification API or dashboard action to check status — this may report 'pending' since DNS propagation is asynchronous, so note that you'll need to poll/re-check verification status periodically (e.g. every 15-30 minutes, or when I ask) until it shows fully verified. If {{vendor}} exposes a verification check endpoint (for example, an operation like verifying a domain's DKIM/SPF records via its API), use it to confirm status rather than guessing.
5. Report back with: the exact DNS records prepared, current verification status, any errors returned by {{vendor}}, and next steps if verification is still pending.

Done looks like: DNS records are drafted and presented for my approval, and once applied, domain verification status is confirmed as fully authenticated via {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard.

growth_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the DNS changes needed to authenticate our transactional email (sent via SendGrid) using {{vendor}} as our DNS/edge platform. If you don't already know them, ask me for: (1) my domain name, (2) confirmation that you have configured credentials to read (not modify yet) DNS records in {{vendor}}, and (3) the SPF and DKIM record values SendGrid's domain authentication page provides for our domain (host, record type, and value for each).

Actions:
1. Retrieve or ask me for the exact SPF and DKIM record values SendGrid requires for domain authentication.
2. Check our current DNS records in {{vendor}} for this domain to see if an SPF record already exists (to avoid duplicates/conflicts) and note any existing entries that would need merging.
3. Prepare a precise list of the DNS records to be added or changed — record type, host/name, value, and TTL — formatted so they can be entered directly into {{vendor}}'s dashboard or created via its API.
4. Note if {{vendor}} needs to also handle TLS certificate issuance or custom domain attachment for any related service endpoints, and flag that as informational only.
5. Do not create, edit, or delete any DNS records yet.

Done looks like: a clear, reviewed draft listing every DNS record needed (SPF, DKIM, and any conflict resolution), with any existing conflicting records called out explicitly, ready for me to approve.

Report back with: the full list of proposed DNS records in a simple table (type, host, value, TTL), any conflicts found in current {{vendor}} DNS settings, and a one-line summary of what SPF and DKIM each accomplish. Then stop for human sign-off — do not apply, submit, or create any records in {{vendor}} until I explicitly approve the change.

growth_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me create transactional email templates using {{vendor}}, the email-API platform I've selected for password resets, receipts, and notifications. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} account credentials context (assume I have configured credentials already), (2) the list of transactional email types I need (e.g., password reset, receipt, welcome, notification), and (3) any existing copy, branding, or design assets for each email type.

Please do the following:
1. For each email type, draft the template content — subject line, body copy, and merge-field placeholders (e.g., {{user_name}}, {{amount}}, {{reset_link}}) — using {{vendor}}'s documented templating language (merge fields, conditionals, loops as needed).
2. Prefer authoring templates as code if {{vendor}} supports a first-party maintained framework (e.g., React Email, MJML, or equivalent); otherwise use {{vendor}}'s native template editor/language, and keep source files organized so they can be version-controlled.
3. Use {{vendor}}'s template management API or dashboard to create each template as a draft (do not publish or activate live sends yet), noting the template ID/name for each.
4. Generate a test/preview render of each template with sample merge-field data to confirm layout and personalization work correctly.
5. Compile a summary checklist showing: template name, purpose, merge fields used, preview status, and template ID.

Done looks like: all required transactional templates exist in {{vendor}} as drafts, each with a working preview and documented merge fields, plus my checklist ready for review.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, do not activate, publish, or trigger any live sends — stop for human sign-off once drafts and the checklist are ready, and report back the template list, IDs, and preview status for my review.

growth_005:n5.prompt:
You are helping me test transactional email delivery for my {{vendor}} account before going live with password resets, receipts, and notifications. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: my {{vendor}} account credentials context (confirm I have configured credentials already), the domain or sender address I've set up for transactional email, and a safe recipient address I own for receiving test messages.
2. Using my configured credentials, send one or more test transactional emails through {{vendor}}'s email-sending API or dashboard test tool. If {{vendor}} offers a sandbox mode, test API key, or dedicated test-sending endpoint that doesn't deliver real mail, use that first to confirm the integration works safely (suitable for CI/agent use) before sending a real test email to my recipient address.
3. Capture the message id or tracking id returned from each send so we can look up delivery status later.
4. Check delivery outcome: confirm the email arrived (or, in sandbox mode, confirm the API accepted it and fired the expected event), and if {{vendor}} exposes per-message event history via the API or dashboard, query it to confirm status (delivered, bounced, opened, clicked, complained).
5. If {{vendor}} supports webhooks for delivery/bounce/complaint events, note whether they're already configured; if not, flag this as a follow-up item rather than configuring it now unless I ask you to.
6. Report back: which send method was used (sandbox/test vs live), the message id(s), the delivery/event status observed, any errors encountered, and whether the account is verified ready for production transactional sends. Do not send bulk or marketing email, and do not modify billing or account settings — only test the sending and tracking capability.
